title: Developing a Multi-Spectral NIR LED-Based Instrument for the Detection of Pesticide Residues Containing Chlorpyrifos-Methyl in Rough, Brown, and Milled Rice
authors: Fatima Rodriguez-Macadaeg; Paul R. Armstrong; Elizabeth B. Maghirang; Erin D. Scully; Daniel L. Brabec; Frank H. Arthur; Arlene D. Adviento-Borbe; Kevin F. Yaptenco; Delfin C. Suministrado
topic: Sparse sequential LEDs; real versus simulated hardware; grouped validation
access: Full publisher text retrieved; PMC intermittently blocked.
setting: Nine LEDs, 850–1550 nm, and InGaAs; five rice varieties; 90 treated subsamples per rice type; repeated repacking.
findings: Mean-centering performed similarly to SNV, MSC and derivatives. Actual held-out-variety prototype results were much poorer than simulated laboratory-spectrometer bands.
lio_application: Benchmark simple centering and leave-one-product/batch-out validation; test actual hardware.
limitations: Pesticide detection differs from food identity. Simulation performance cannot be assigned to the actual prototype.

title: Low-cost VIS/NIR range hand-held and portable photospectrometer and evaluation of machine learning algorithms for classification performance
authors: Saddam Heydarov; Musa Aydin; Cagri Faydaci; Suha Tuna; Sadullah Ozturk
topic: Sparse18-channel food identity; white powder discrimination
access: Publisher returned 403; complete author-uploaded original PDF read on ResearchGate; publication metadata verified.
setting: AS7265x, 410–940 nm; nine powder/flake foods; 150 measurements per type; independent preparations unclear.
findings: Mean signatures with SD show subtle powder differences; normalized SVM/CNN distinguish classes using random measurement splits.
lio_application: Plot band means and replicate spread, then multivariate scores.
limitations: The reported 97% SVM result does not demonstrate unseen-day or product-lot generalization; bands differ from LIO.

title: Handheld Spectral Sensing Devices Should Not Mislead Consumers as Far as Non-Authentic Food Is Concerned: A Case Study with Adulteration of Milk Powder
authors: Thierry Delatour; Florian Becker; Julius Krause; Roman Romero; Robin Gruna; Thomas Längle; Alexandre Panchaud
access: PubMed abstract and primary indexed fragments retrieved; direct full text blocked by 429/PMC challenge. Online 2021; volume 11 (2022).
setting: Eight sensors; dry- and wet-blended skimmed milk powders; three adulterants.
findings: SIMCA/OPLS found inadequate detection and specificity around 5% supplementation for many sensors.
lio_application: Treat embeddings as exploratory; show confusion and held-out errors.
limitations: Full sample allocation was not verified. No performance estimate transfers to LIO.

title: A Portable Spectrometric System for Quantitative Prediction of the Soluble Solids Content of Apples with a Pre-calibrated Multispectral Sensor Chipset
authors: Nhut-Thanh Tran; Masayuki Fukuzawa
access: Primary indexed methods and abstract retrieved; direct PMC challenge and publisher PDF content-type failure.
setting: AS7265x, 410–940 nm, versus dispersive spectrometer; 80 apples, two sides each, 20 scans averaged.
findings: Fixed 20 mm geometry; an 18% gray reference every four samples; relative normalization before log transform and regression.
lio_application: Collect reference measurements and control geometry before chemometrics.
limitations: Fruit-level split allocation was not verified; the published ratio should not automatically be called absolute reflectance.

title: A Simplified, Light Emitting Diode (LED) Based, Modular System to be Used for the Rapid Evaluation of Fruit and Vegetable Quality: Development and Validation on Dye Solutions
authors: Raffaele Civelli; Valentina Giovenzana; Ezio Naldi; Riccardo Guidetti; Roberto Oberti
topic: Sequential LED calibration and detector linearity
access: Extensive primary indexed passages retrieved; direct PMC challenge and publisher timeout.
setting: Four-LED modular reflectometer; calibrated diffuse standards; dye solutions in a fixed PTFE-backed holder.
findings: Channel-specific stimulus/gain curves and repeated acquisitions characterize sensitivity and repeatability.
lio_application: Check channel linearity, ranges and reference geometry before interpreting ratios.
limitations: Validation used dye solutions, not food discrimination.

title: Quantitative assessment of adulteration of coconut oil using transmittance multispectral imaging
authors: Sanjaya Herath; Hashan Kavinga Weerasooriya; Don Yasiru Lakshan Ranasinghe; Wele Gedara Chaminda Bandara; Vijitha Rohana Herath; Roshan Indika Godaliyadda; Mervyn Parakrama Bandara Ekanayake; Terrence Madhujith
setting: Nine LED bands with published dominant wavelengths405–950nm (nominal emitting-band envelope375–1000nm), monochrome camera; palm/coconut oil mixtures;15trials per level;16new-batch validation samples.
findings: Mean band profiles illustrate mixture changes; supervised FDA and distribution distance estimate mixture level.
lio_application: Band profiles and new-batch validation are useful patterns.
limitations: Transmission differs from reflectance. Pixels are not independent foods; complex Gaussian modeling is unnecessary for LIO V1.

title: Feasibility assessment of a low-cost visible spectroscopy-based prototype for monitoring polyphenol extraction in fermenting musts
authors: Gianmarco Alfieri; Margherita Modesti; Andrea Bellincontro; Francesco Renzi; Jose Luis Aleixandre-Tudo
topic: Low-cost sparse food device versus benchtop reality
access: Full PMC text retrieved. Online 2024; issue 2025.
setting: Eight channels, 460–680 nm; three grape varieties; fermentation trajectories; ten readings averaged; benchtop comparison.
findings: Autoscaled PCR with Venetian-blind cross-validation gave modest prototype prediction; authors acknowledge incomplete reliability.
lio_application: Show trajectories and uncertainty; collect chemical reference labels before biochemical interpretation.
limitations: Fixed-cuvette transmission; no independent-vintage validation, and repeated fermentation measurements complicate validation.

title: IoT System for Gluten Prediction in Flour Samples Using NIRS Technology, Deep and Machine Learning Techniques
authors: Oscar Jossa-Bastidas; Ainhoa Osa-Sanchez; Leire Bravo-Lamas; Begonya García-Zapirain
topic: Powder presentation; many spectra from few source products
access: Primary indexed PDF methods and abstract retrieved; direct publisher access blocked.
setting: DLP NIRNano; rye, corn and oat flours, two brands each, control and gluten addition; 12,053 reported readings.
findings: The authors leveled the powder surface after rough surfaces produced inconsistent measurements; a dark printed fixture held the sensor rigid.
lio_application: Record packing and physical-source hierarchy; distinguish readings from independent foods.
limitations: Dense DLP spectra differ from sparse LEDs; independent-group validation was not verified.

title: TinyML-Sensor for Shelf Life Estimation of Fresh Date Fruits
authors: Ramasamy Srinivasagan; Maged Mohammed; Ali Alzahrani
setting: AS7265x; Khalas dates; four packaging treatments, two temperatures; longitudinal age labels.
findings: Channel profiles and feature plots visualize progression; modeling used a random 60/20/20 split.
lio_application: Show aging trajectories with preparation and storage metadata.
limitations: No demonstrated unseen-harvest validation. Elapsed age is not universal spoilage or safety; acquisition descriptions include ambiguities.

title: Penetration Depth Measurement of Near-Infrared Hyperspectral Imaging Light for Milk Powder
authors: Min Huang; Moon S. Kim; Kuanglin Chao; Jianwei Qin; Changyeun Mo; Carlos Esquerre; Stephen Delwiche; Qibing Zhu
topic: Powder fill depth and backing effects
setting: NIR HSI, 937.5–1653.7 nm; eight milk-powder products, 152 physical plates; controlled powder depths.
findings: Underlying-material detection deteriorated with thickness; mean spectra could hide it. Physical plates were held out, with cross-validation blocked by product.
lio_application: Test fill depth and backing alongside food identity.
limitations: Dense HSI differs from LIO; its specific 2 mm recommendation cannot be transferred.

title: ANOVA-simultaneous component analysis (ASCA): a new tool for analyzing designed metabolomics data
authors: Age K. Smilde; Jeroen J. Jansen; Huub C. J. Hoefsloot; Robert-Jan A. N. Lamers; Jan van der Greef; Marieke E. Timmerman
access: Primary abstract; publisher full text inaccessible
setting: Original method illustrated with time×dose metabolomics
findings: ASCA decomposes multivariate design effects and applies component analysis to improve factor-specific interpretation.
lio_application: Use food/day effect matrices on run-level features after balanced collection.
limitations: Cannot separate confounded food/day factors or automatically handle nested technical repeats. 2007 erratum corrects an inappropriate corroboration statement, not method validity.

title: ANOVA-Simultaneous Component analysis modelling of low-level-fused spectroscopic data: A food chemistry case-study
authors: P. Firmani; R. Vitale; C. Ruckebusch; F. Marini
access: Primary abstract and author-manuscript metadata; full publisher text inaccessible
setting: Cheddar cheese, Raman+MIR, storage time×temperature
findings: ASCA on fused spectroscopy examined ripening effects of time, temperature, and interaction.
lio_application: Direct food precedent for design-effect visualization across distinct measurement blocks.
limitations: Not sparse LED reflectance; no LIO-specific channel or model-superiority claim.

title: Multivariate Functional Principal Component Analysis for Data Observed on Different (Dimensional) Domains
authors: Clara Happ; Sonja Greven
setting: Original theory, simulations and neuroimaging application
findings: Joint functional components use univariate finite basis expansions; accommodates sparse/noisy functions and positive function-level weights.
lio_application: Represent each valid detector-hole pair as x_j(height); visualize sample scores and channel-height eigenfunctions.
limitations: No LIO/food validation; smoothing, weighting and covariance estimates need sufficient independent runs.

title: Curve Registration
authors: J. O. Ramsay; Xiaochun Li
access: Publisher-indexed summary; full article endpoint failed
setting: Original method with illustrative curve data
findings: Smooth monotone argument transformations distinguish horizontal/domain from vertical/range variation.
lio_application: Keep height shifts separate from amplitude; constrain and record any justified alignment.
limitations: LIO physical-height shifts are not automatically nuisance; do not align by food labels or erase peak shifts.

title: Some Mathematical Notes on Three-Mode Factor Analysis
authors: Ledyard R. Tucker
access: Publisher abstract and metadata, not full article
setting: Original mathematical methods
findings: Extends factor/component analysis to three-mode structured arrays.
lio_application: Flexible comparative model for sample×valid-channel×height interactions.
limitations: Additional parameters and rotational interpretation; components are not automatically pure ingredients.

title: A new efficient method for determining the number of components in PARAFAC models
authors: Rasmus Bro; Henk A. L. Kiers
setting: Original diagnostic with examples and simulations
findings: Core consistency examines appropriateness of restricted multiway structure as rank increases; authors note incomplete theoretical understanding.
lio_application: If CP is explored, combine structural diagnostics with residuals, multistart stability and held-out-run reconstruction.
limitations: No universal cutoff proves LIO physical truth or correct chemical factors.

title: Scalable tensor factorizations for incomplete data
authors: Evrim Acar; Daniel M. Dunlavy; Tamara G. Kolda; Morten Mørup
setting: Original optimization method, simulations, EEG and network traffic
findings: Weighted least-squares fits observed entries while ignoring missing ones.
lio_application: Mask genuine missing measurements rather than zero-fill if fitting multiway models.
limitations: Structural blinds are not hidden food spectra to reconstruct; random-missing results do not validate filling entire unsupported LIO bands.

title: Centering, scaling, and transformations: improving the biological information content of metabolomics data
authors: Robert A. van den Berg; Huub C. J. Hoefsloot; Johan A. Westerhuis; Age K. Smilde; Mariët J. van der Werf
access: Full primary text retrieved via indexed PMC result.
setting: Empirical metabolomics preprocessing comparison.
findings: Scaling and transformations changed PCA feature ranking and technical-error influence; weak-value inflation can amplify error.
lio_application: Compare justified scaling branches using independent preparation/day reproducibility; qualify channels before autoscaling.
limitations: Metabolomics, not sparse LED food data; no universally best LIO scaling is established.

title: The biplot graphic display of matrices with application to principal component analysis
authors: K. R. Gabriel
setting: Original matrix visualization method.
findings: Joint row/column markers represent a rank-two approximation through inner products.
lio_application: Link food scores to channel loadings/contributions rather than present unlabeled islands.
limitations: Biplot scaling and low-dimensional approximation govern geometric interpretation; abstract-only inspection.

title: FactoMineR: An R Package for Multivariate Analysis
authors: Sébastien Lê; Julie Josse; François Husson
access: Primary journal landing page retrieved; PDF route attempted.
setting: Original software/method paper.
findings: Exploratory analysis can retain variable partitions and supplementary individuals/variables.
lio_application: Use detector blocks and supplementary day/fill metadata; assess MFA as a V2 comparison.
limitations: Does not establish superiority over a specified weighted PCA or demonstrate LIO results.

title: A Sequential Algorithm for Multiblock Orthogonal Projections to Latent Structures
authors: Bradley Worley; Robert Powers
setting: Derivations, synthetic data and joint NMR/MS data.
findings: Normalized CPCA-W superscores can equal concatenated-PCA scores; block architecture alone does not imply additional information.
lio_application: State variable scaling/block weights and inspect detector contributions.
limitations: Supervised extensions are not required for initial exploratory food maps; distinct acquisition platform.

title: Cluster analysis and display of genome-wide expression patterns
authors: Michael B. Eisen; Paul T. Spellman; Patrick O. Brown; David Botstein
access: Full primary indexed text retrieved; later direct open hit CAPTCHA.
setting: Yeast and human gene-expression data.
findings: Similarity ordering combined with colored measurements exposes patterns; correlation emphasizes shape rather than magnitude.
lio_application: Pair sample-feature and pairwise-distance heatmaps with selectable distance/ordering.
limitations: Methodological transfer, not spectroscopy validation; a dendrogram is not evidence of a true food taxonomy.

title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE
authors: Laurens van der Maaten; Geoffrey Hinton
setting: Original method and diverse high-dimensional benchmark datasets.
findings: Neighborhood similarities are embedded using a KL objective and low-dimensional heavy-tailed distribution.
lio_application: Optional nonlinear neighborhood view using already qualified LIO features.
limitations: Not direct LIO/food evidence; does not establish a universal minimum N or validate chemical distances.

title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction
authors: Leland McInnes; John Healy; James Melville
access: Author preprint abstract retrieved; version revised 2020.
setting: Original topological neighbor-embedding method.
findings: Constructs a neighbor graph and optimizes its low-dimensional representation.
lio_application: Possible later neighborhood panel with fixed features, seed and sensitivity checks.
limitations: Preprint; original global-structure claims should be qualified by independent comparisons.

title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection
authors: Leland McInnes; John Healy; Nathaniel Saul; Lukas Großberger
setting: Original software paper.
findings: Documents the UMAP implementation and archival provenance.
lio_application: Record implementation version and cite software separately when used.
limitations: Same method family as O8a, not independent food-performance validation.

title: Attraction-Repulsion Spectrum in Neighbor Embeddings
authors: Jan Niklas Böhm; Philipp Berens; Dmitry Kobak
access: Primary JMLR and author-arXiv abstracts retrieved.
setting: Empirical/theoretical comparison of neighbor embeddings.
findings: Attraction/repulsion balance trades continuous structure against discrete clusters; connects UMAP with modified t-SNE.
lio_application: Require seed/parameter stability and original-space checks rather than prettiest-island selection.
limitations: Generic benchmark evidence, not sparse multispectral food validation; final JMLR title differs from early preprint.

title: How to Use t-SNE Effectively
authors: Martin Wattenberg; Fernanda Viégas; Ian Johnson
setting: Synthetic controlled datasets and parameter experiments.
findings: t-SNE can equalize cluster sizes, distort intercluster distances and create apparent clumps in random data.
lio_application: Never infer food variance or chemical distance from island area/spacing; show sensitivity panels.
limitations: Original methodological demonstrations, not empirical food separation.

title: Initialization is critical for preserving global data structure in both t-SNE and UMAP
authors: Dmitry Kobak; George C. Linderman
access: Final metadata verified in PubMed; experimental content read in 2019 author preprint DOI10.1101/2019.12.19.877522.
setting: Reanalysis of high-dimensional biological visualization benchmarks.
findings: Matching informative/random initialization changes the apparent global-structure comparison.
lio_application: Avoid claiming universal UMAP superiority; record initialization when comparing maps.
limitations: Publisher full text blocked; inspected experimental version was earlier author preprint.

title: Linearization and Scatter-Correction for Near-Infrared Reflectance Spectra of Meat
authors: P. Geladi; D. MacDougall; H. Martens
setting: Dense near-infrared diffuse-reflectance spectra of meat; PLS fat calibration.
findings: MSC improved response-linearized fat calibration and simplified models; extracted scatter coefficients correlated with fat.
lio_application: Keep amplitude/scattering information or correction parameters rather than treating all scatter as irrelevant.
limitations: Original publisher abstract inspected; full text unavailable. Dense-spectral quantitative calibration does not validate sparse LIO preprocessing.

title: Standard Normal Variate Transformation and De-trending of Near-Infrared Diffuse Reflectance Spectra
authors: R. J. Barnes; M. S. Dhanoa; S. J. Lister
setting: Dense near-infrared diffuse-reflectance spectra affected by particle size, scatter and baseline variation.
findings: Introduces per-spectrum SNV for multiplicative scatter and polynomial detrending for baseline variation.
lio_application: Evaluate SNV as a separate shape-emphasizing representation; retain an amplitude-preserving branch.
limitations: Original abstract only. No validation for mixing raw detector gains, sparse broadband LED features or weak near-flat LIO blocks.

title: Extended multiplicative signal correction and spectral interference subtraction: New preprocessing methods for near infrared spectroscopy
authors: H. Martens; E. Stark
setting: NIR spectra of toluene/benzene/xylene mixtures with simulated scattering.
findings: Introduces model-based path-length/scatter correction and subtraction of known spectral interferences.
lio_application: Use physical nuisance knowledge before adding correction terms; consider EMSC only after controlled nuisance experiments.
limitations: Original abstract inspected. Mixture simulation and dense NIR do not establish identifiable models for LIO’s few valid SWIR channels.

title: Light scattering and light absorbance separated by extended multiplicative signal correction. Application to near-infrared transmission analysis of powder mixtures
authors: H. Martens; J. P. Nielsen; S. B. Engelsen
setting: Diffuse NIR transmission spectra of wheat gluten/starch powder mixtures.
findings: Standard MSC removed too much analyte information; EMSC more effectively separated scattering and absorbance.
lio_application: Retain minimally corrected features and validate corrections on independent food preparations rather than assume MSC helps.
limitations: Original abstract only; transmission geometry differs from LIO diffuse reflectance. The winning correction cannot be transferred automatically.

title: The Use of Constituent Spectra and Weighting in Extended Multiplicative Signal Correction in Infrared Spectroscopy
authors: J. H. Solheim; B. Zimmermann; V. Tafintseva; S. Dzurendová; V. Shapaval; A. Kohler
setting: Simulations and FTIR studies of fungi, growth media and beef-tissue microscopy.
findings: Normalization changes the relative-composition target; chemical information can enter baseline terms; collinear constituents can destabilize correction.
lio_application: Label what normalization removes; retain correction parameters; avoid elaborate EMSC on sparse channels.
limitations: FTIR/ATR/microscopy data support methodological principles, not a tested LIO correction recipe.

title: Preprocessing Strategies for Sparse Infrared Spectroscopy: A Case Study on Cartilage Diagnostics
authors: V. Tafintseva; T. A. Lintvedt; J. H. Solheim; B. Zimmermann; H. U. Rehman; V. Virtanen; R. Shaikh; E. Nippolainen; I. Afara; S. Saarakkala; L. Rieppo; P. Krebs; P. Fomina; B. Mizaikoff; A. Kohler
setting: Measured/simulated MIR-ATR cartilage spectra reduced to seven variables; PLSDA including leave-one-cadaver-out validation.
findings: Simple offset/peak normalization or MSC performed favorably; added EMSC terms often degraded classification; quadratic EMSC was rejected for insufficient degrees of freedom.
lio_application: Validate preprocessing on sparse data directly and limit correction complexity.
limitations: Cartilage MIR-ATR differs from scattering food reflectance. Its reference bands and winning normalization must not be transferred to LIO.

title: Calibration of a Hyper-Spectral Imaging System Using a Low-Cost Reference
authors: M. S. Shaikh; K. Jaferzadeh; B. Thörnberg; J. Casselgren
topic: PTFE reference; dark correction; relative reflectance
setting: InGaAs 900–1700 nm hyperspectral camera; road materials under varying illumination; solid PTFE reference.
findings: Reference calibration reduced illumination-dependent variation before PCA; relative reflectance was distinguished from traceably calibrated true reflectance.
lio_application: Test same-channel reference-relative responses and verify denominator strength/stability; use honest relative units.
limitations: Not food data or LIO geometry; does not establish an arbitrary PTFE tile as a traceable reflectance standard.

title: LED-based, real-time, hyperspectral imaging device
authors: N. Modir; M. Shahedi; J. Dormer; L. Ma; B. Fei
topic: Discrete LED illumination; reference correction; geometry
setting: Eighteen individually controlled LEDs at 405–910 nm, monochrome camera, adjustable sample stage and tissue imaging.
findings: Band-dependent illumination variation arose from LED arrangement; changing imaging depth affected spectral signatures; white/dark calibration and shape normalization were assessed.
lio_application: Control/record geometry and evaluate reference correction over the height sweep; retain amplitude alongside normalized profiles.
limitations: Tissue camera system differs from dual-detector food scans; min–max-normalized plots discard brightness and do not validate quantitative amplitude preservation.

title: Rapid identification of coffee species and origin using affordable multi-channel spectral sensor combined with machine learning
authors: D. Sagita; S. Widodo; S. S. Mardjan; P. B. Purwandoko; Suparlan; H. Hariadi; S. Darniadi
topic: Compact-sensor food fingerprints; raw versus pretreatment
setting: AS7265X 410–940 nm coffee species/origin measurements with 18/24/30 features, PCA exploration and multiple classifiers.
findings: The abstract reports that tested pretreatments did not improve classification; raw features performed well.
lio_application: Keep raw/minimally corrected sparse-channel features as a baseline rather than mandate SNV/MSC.
limitations: Complete original abstract retrieved through indexed search; full text unavailable. Independent preparation/day/lot splitting was not assessed; reported accuracy is not expected LIO performance.

title: The Effect of Light Intensity, Sensor Height, and Spectral Pre-Processing Methods When Using NIR Spectroscopy to Identify Different Allergen-Containing Powdered Foods
authors: Ahmed Rady; Joel Fischer; Stuart Reeves; Brian Logan; Nicholas James Watson
setting: 53 powdered/flake/seed materials; 401 channels from1550–1950nm; six measurement heights and seven light intensities; five scan replicates per setting.
findings: Height and light level changed PCA/classification. SNV/MSC improved some settings. The instrument recorded white/dark references by height.
lio_application: Choose height experimentally, preserve height-response data, and compare simple preprocessing under a crossed design.
limitations: Dense spectra are unlike LIO; scan replicates do not establish independent-lot generalization. Pure-food classification does not validate trace-allergen detection.

title: Multispectral Portable Fibre-Optic Reflectometer for the Classification of the Origin of Chicken Eggshells in the Case of Mycoplasma synoviae Infections
authors: Anna Pakuła; Wojciech Żołnowski; Sławomir Paśko; Olimpia Kursa; Paweł Marć; Leszek R. Jaroszewicz
setting: Six sequential LED bands; photodetector reflectometry; controlled distance and collimator comparison.
findings: In the uncollimated configuration a2mm distance increase reduced signal33–47%; collimation substantially reduced distance sensitivity. Reference normalization compensated differing emitter powers.
lio_application: Treat height/spot geometry as a major potential confound; compare matching reference and specimen geometry.
limitations: Fiber-coupled eggshell apparatus differs from LIO. Its distance-effect sizes and classifier metrics are not LIO predictions.

title: Evaluation of Steady-State and Time-Resolved Fluorescence Spectroscopy as a Method for Assessing the Impact of Photo-Oxidation on Refined Soybean Oils
authors: Carla Regina Borges Lopes et al.
setting: Soybean oil fluorescence with373,405,500nm excitation; photo-oxidation experiments.
findings: 405nm excitation can produce longer-wavelength fluorescence in edible oil; emission includes visible bands.
lio_application: LIO's broadband OPT101 may collect fluorescence as well as reflected excitation under UV/violet illumination; investigate before assigning a pure-reflectance interpretation.
limitations: Potential LIO contribution is an inference, not measured here. Emission-resolved instrumentation differs from LIO.

title: Studies on the influence of uniformity of particle size of powder, tapping and sample replacement for diffusion reflectance quantitative NIR spectrometric analysis
authors: T. Sakamoto; Y. Fujimaki; Y. Hiyama
setting: Ground and unground lactose-monohydrate powders; tapping and sample replacement; NIR diffuse reflectance.
findings: Physical presentation affected repeatability; preprocessing changed confidence intervals and was not uniformly beneficial.
lio_application: Distinguish same-cup repeats from replacement/repacking controls; judge preprocessing against preparation variation.
limitations: Pharmaceutical lactose experiment, not heterogeneous foods or sparse LEDs; no DOI verified.

title: Assessment of PLSDA cross validation
authors: J. A. Westerhuis; H. C. J. Hoefsloot; S. Smit; D. J. Vis; A. K. Smilde; E. J. J. van Velzen; J. P. M. van Duijnhoven; F. A. van Dorsten
setting: Method simulations and human NMR metabolomics
findings: Arbitrary groups can separate in fitted PLSDA scores; proper cross-model validation/permutation avoids optimism.
lio_application: Use unsupervised profiles first; validate selected pipelines at independent preparation/material level.
limitations: Not a food optical experiment; fitted score separation does not establish prediction.

title: Double-check: validation of diagnostic statistics for PLS-DA models in metabolomics studies
authors: E. Szymańska; E. Saccenti; A. K. Smilde; J. A. Westerhuis
topic: Nested PLSDA validation and performance statistics
setting: NMR/UPLC-MS datasets with known effects
findings: Tuning complexity and assessing performance require separate loops; statistic choice changes sensitivity.
lio_application: Height/channel/preprocessing selection belongs inside validation when claiming generalization.
limitations: No universal LIO sample count or quality threshold follows.

title: Bias in error estimation when using cross-validation for model selection
authors: S. Varma; R. Simon
access: Primary text retrieved; subsequent anti-bot challenge
setting: High-dimensional classification simulations
findings: Reporting the CV result that selected the model produces optimistic error estimates.
lio_application: Keep held-out material/day for testing chosen preprocessing, heights and models.
limitations: Microarray setting; transfer is statistical, not optical.

title: Cross-validation of component models: a critical look at current methods
authors: R. Bro; K. Kjeldahl; A. K. Smilde; H. A. L. Kiers
setting: Methodological assessment
findings: Many component-model CV implementations do not preserve prediction independence.
lio_application: Separate exploratory PCA, reconstruction validation and held-out identity prediction.
limitations: Full text not independently checked; descriptive all-data PCA remains legitimate.

title: Reduction of repeatability error for analysis of variance–Simultaneous Component Analysis (REP-ASCA): Application to NIR spectroscopy on coffee sample
authors: M. Ryckewaert; N. Gorretta; F. Henriot; F. Marini; J.-M. Roger
setting: NIR coffee experiment
findings: Physical repeatability error can dominate factor analysis; repeated-control-informed projection reduced it.
lio_application: Collect controlled reload/repack sets and test nuisance effects separately.
limitations: Full methods/sample count not verified; removing physical effects may remove LIO food signal.

title: Quality Assessment of Reconstructed Cow, Camel and Mare Milk Powders by Near-Infrared Spectroscopy and Chemometrics
authors: M. Majadi; A. Barkó; A. Varga-Tóth; Z. S. Maukenovna; D. Z. Batirkhanovna; S. Dilora; M. Lukacs; T. Kaszab; Z. Mednyánszky; Z. Kovacs
setting: Reconstructed milk; dense transflectance NIR; varied type/concentration/temperature
findings: Random-order collection; consecutive scans of a preparation kept together in partitions.
lio_application: Record physical factors and group technical scans.
limitations: Dense commercial NIR geometry; reported accuracy/derivative processing does not transfer to LIO.

title: Distance-Based Tests for Homogeneity of Multivariate Dispersions
authors: M. J. Anderson
setting: Statistical method and ecological simulations/examples
findings: Distance-based centroid/median spread tests separate a dispersion question.
lio_application: Show within-food spread and individual preparations alongside centers.
limitations: Hierarchy-aware permutations required; not food-specific.

title: Distance-based multivariate analyses confound location and dispersion effects
authors: D. I. Warton; S. T. Wright; Y. Wang
setting: Ecological abundance analysis
findings: Mean–variance misspecification can confound center and spread effects in distance analysis.
lio_application: Inspect distance/scaling sensitivity and unequal food spread.
limitations: ADC counts are not ecological Poisson counts; do not transplant count-data GLMs.

title: XAI-Supported Electronic Tongue for Estimating Milk Composition and Adulteration Indicators
authors: A. Ç. Seçkin; M. Ekici; T. Akcan; F. Soygazi; H. Gürsoy Demir
setting: AS7265x milk; 190 reported undiluted/diluted preparations
findings: Means of three readings modelled; shuffled fivefold and prepared-sample LOO, no reported parent/brand/day grouping.
lio_application: Use hardware feasibility, not field-generalization claims, as evidence.
limitations: Related dilution leakage unresolved, not proven; Table1 sums195 versus reported190; augmentation is physical dilution.
